stage_description: Young adulthood runs from 1 to 6 years (AAHA/AAFP 2021). The cat is in its prime, physically and socially mature. Indoor cats at this stage are especially prone to weight gain and boredom when under-stimulated, while cats with outdoor access face injuries and infections that shorten their lives considerably. The main goal is to maintain a healthy weight, activity, and a stable routine.
nutrition: A quality adult food, usually two meals a day or portioned feeding; control portions, since obesity is one of the most common problems in indoor cats. Ensure adequate water intake — wet food helps — and make any diet change gradual.
activity: Daily 15–20 minute play sessions that mimic hunting, plus environmental enrichment: vertical shelves, scratching posts, hiding spots, and window views. Activity prevents boredom, obesity, and stress-related behavior and urinary problems.
veterinary_check_frequency: A routine exam once a year with scheduled boosters, weight checks, and parasite control. The annual visit records a healthy cat's normal values for future comparison.
dental_care: Regular toothbrushing with cat-specific paste and an oral assessment at the annual exam. Dental and gum disease is common in cats and often hidden, so preventive monitoring matters.
warning_signs: Changes in appetite or thirst, weight loss or gain, changes in behavior, litter-box frequency, or urination. Noticeable departures from the cat's normal state warrant a veterinary visit.
disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and does not replace consultation with a veterinarian.
